concepts.title: Arithmetic Expressions and Their Values
concepts.definition: An arithmetic expression is a phrase made of numbers joined by operations like +, -, x and division, such as 18 divided by 3; every expression has a value that it evaluates to.
concepts.key_idea: An expression is a calculation in waiting: carrying out its operations in the right way gives its single value.
question_patterns: what is an arithmetic expression give two examples
find the value of 18 divided by 3
write an expression for the total of 25 and 40
what does it mean to evaluate an expression
make an expression whose value is 20
how is an expression different from an equation

solution_steps.explain: Say the rule in your own words.
Work it out on one small example from the chapter.
Verify by reversing or re-checking, then conclude.

concepts.title: Order of Operations
concepts.definition: Expressions must be evaluated in a fixed order: brackets first, then multiplication and division from left to right, and finally addition and subtraction from left to right, so that everyone gets the same value.
concepts.key_idea: Order is the grammar of arithmetic: without a fixed order, one expression would have many values.
question_patterns: evaluate 10 + 4 x 2 with correct order
why is the order of operations needed
evaluate 20 - 6 divided by 2
which comes first in an expression multiplication or addition
evaluate 8 + 12 divided by 4 x 3 step by step
find two classmates getting different values and fix the mistake

solution_steps.explain: Carry out every multiplication and division before adding.
Add the remaining terms to get the value.

concepts.title: Brackets Change Everything
concepts.definition: Brackets promote a part of an expression to first place: (7 + 5) x 3 evaluates the sum before multiplying, and expressions with and without brackets can give different values.
concepts.key_idea: Brackets are the loudest signal in an expression: whatever they hold is settled before anything else.
question_patterns: evaluate (7 + 5) x 3
compare 7 + 5 x 3 and (7 + 5) x 3
why do brackets get first priority
put brackets in 9 - 2 x 4 to make the value 28
evaluate 36 divided by (2 + 4)

solution_steps.explain: Say the rule in your own words.

Verify by reversing or re-checking, then conclude.

concepts.title: Expressions from Everyday Situations
concepts.definition: Everyday stories turn into expressions: a shop bill, a cricket score or a journey total can each be written as numbers joined by operations before any calculation is done.
concepts.key_idea: Translating words to expressions and back is two-way: each story has an expression, each expression has a story.
question_patterns: write an expression for 5 notebooks at 40 rupees each plus 15 rupees for a pen
make a story for the expression 12 x 4 + 8
write the expression for a score of two fours and two sixes in cricket
